steps.body: A prism is layers of the same base stacked up. Each layer is a complete copy, so the height MULTIPLIES rather than adds.
steps.narration: A prism is layers of the same base stacked up. Each layer is a complete copy, so the height MULTIPLIES rather than adds.

widget.prompt: Build four identical layers of 12 cubes each.
widget.successFeedback: 48 cubes — four complete copies of the 12-cube base.
widget.partialFeedback: Every layer is a full copy of the base: build each bar to 12.

predict.prompt: Base of 12, four layers — 16 cubes or 48?
predict.reveal: Each layer repeats the whole base, so four layers hold four twelves; 16 comes from adding 12 and 4 instead of repeating the base.

cml.actionGoal: Build one layer, then count how many layers the height stacks for g5v layers.
invariants: Volume is a count of unit cubes, and a prism organises that count into identical layers: the base area counts one layer and the height counts the layers, which is why g5v layers is a product rather than a sum.
misconceptions: Adding the three dimensions instead of multiplying, stopping at the base area, or adding a removed notch instead of subtracting it.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the height doubled but the base stayed the same, what would happen to the cube count?

widget.prompt: A box has a base of 12 cubes and is 4 layers tall. How does the height act? Choose a new reason.

options.label: It repeats the base 4 times, giving 48 cubes
options.feedback: Correct — each layer is a full copy of the base, so the height multiplies rather than adds.

options.label: It adds 4 cubes to the base, giving 16
options.feedback: Adding would treat the height as a handful of extra cubes; each layer copies the whole base.

options.label: It has no effect on the count
options.feedback: Stacking layers is exactly what turns a flat base into a solid with volume.

options.label: It halves the base each layer
options.feedback: Every layer is identical to the base; nothing shrinks as the stack rises.

cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the height doubled but the base stayed the same, what would happen to the cube count?

options.feedback: Correct — each pour repeats the whole base, so 4 layers multiply the base count by 4.

options.feedback: Each additional pour adds another full layer, so the count keeps growing with height.

options.label: A shrinking fraction of the base for every additional pour
options.feedback: Nothing shrinks — every layer, however many are poured, matches the base exactly.
